text:
lina: quick flag - raven-lite int8 canary shows an uptick in funcall JSON parsing errors (3.4%). Want to propose a short rescue + small experiment comparing constrained re-ask vs deterministic decode.

ben: interested. deterministic decode (top_k=1 / beam=1) should reduce sampling noise but might harm diversity. For funcalls JSON needs determinism more than diversity.

meera: sample failure from logs: 
```
{
  "operation": "create_incident",
  "params": {
    "title": "High CPU"
  } // <-- stray comment

```

josh: comment token + missing closing brace. int8 seems to stochastically inject these artifacts more often.

lina: proposed rescue pipeline: (1) cheap repair (strip JS-style comments, drop trailing commas, auto-close small brace imbalances), (2) if repair fails, branch experiment: for half of repaired failures do a constrained re-ask (temp=0.0), for the other half do deterministic decode (top_k=1) on the same int8 model. If still invalid after branch, fallback to fp16. Track which branch wins.

ben: telemetry we need: `rescue_branch=reask|deterministic`, `repair_applied=true|false`, `parse_outcome=ok|repaired|fallback`, `latency_ms`, `token_cost_delta`. Also capture `input_signature` hash to group similar prompts.

meera: bench-bot snapshot 2026-03-21T15:34Z:
- int8 baseline parse_fail=3.38% (n=12,600)
- repair-only reduced to 1.12% (repair fixed ~66.9% of fails)
- after branching experiment (n=2,400 repaired failures split 50/50):
  - re-ask (temp=0.0) success_rate=74.5%
  - deterministic decode (top_k=1) success_rate=69.8%
- fallback_fp16 rate across experiment: 0.03%
- median added latency re-ask=+24ms, deterministic=+3ms; token overhead re-ask=+18 tokens (on average), deterministic=+0 tokens

josh: interesting - deterministic is cheaper and faster but slightly less effective. Re-ask recovers more but costs tokens/time. Decision depends on SLAs and customer cost sensitivity.

lina: proposal for rollout: enable repair-only globally for canary (10% traffic). Run the branch experiment for a week on repaired failure traffic only to collect statistically significant results, then pick a default: prefer deterministic decode for latency-sensitive customers, and re-ask for customers with strict reliability SLAs (configurable per-customer).

ben: add per-customer opt-in header `x-rescue-preference: deterministic|reask|fallback-only`. Default `auto` will map to deterministic for free-tier and re-ask for enterprise.

meera: also suggest adding a low-cost verification step before invoking funcall: quick JSON schema validator on a best-effort parse that runs in <1ms to avoid expensive fallbacks for trivial noise.

bench-bot: action summary recorded: deploy repair-only canary, start 7-day branch experiment on repaired failures, add telemetry fields and dashboard slices for `rescue_branch` vs parse_success, add per-customer header flag.

josh: I'll prototype the deterministic decode wrapper and latency budget check.

lina: i'll implement repair heuristics and wire telemetry. Ben, can you draft the customer header spec?

ben: on it. No blockers from infra.

meera: agreed. If deterministic wins for most, we can keep re-ask as a paid premium reliability option.

lina: thanks all 680. will post canary results in this thread.
